```{r installing and calling Rpackages}
install.packages("Rsampling")
install.packages("vegan")
install.packages("pbapply")
install.packages("ggplot2")
install.packages("glmmTMB")
install.packages("DHARMa")
install.packages("dplyr")
install.packages("tidyr")
install.packages("emmeans")
```

```{r calling Rpackages}
library(Rsampling)
library(vegan)
library(pbapply)
library(ggplot2)
library(glmmTMB)
library(DHARMa)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(emmeans)
```

```{r importing the data}
data_raw <- read.table("~/Jussara_autotomy/data/raw/data.tsv", header = T, stringsAsFactors = T, sep='\t')
data <- data_raw[, -c(10, 11, 12)]
```

```{r resuming the data}

```

Information that we discussed in the reunion: 
We need to make a descriptive analyses (glmm) comparing if the autotomy differ between: population (which is the collectors because they collected only 1 time each year in four different years ps: the data is temporally organized - 2002, 2009, 2011, 2012); type of leg (1,2,3 or 4); and side (right or left)

```{r transforming into a long table}
df_long <- data %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = r1:l4,
               names_to = "leg_id",
               values_to = "autotomy") %>%
  mutate(
    side = ifelse(grepl("^r", leg_id), "right", "left"),
    leg = gsub("[rl]", "", leg_id)
  )
```
sim, nessa parte eu pedi ajuda pro chat gpt, mas conferindo a df_long, ele me parece certo

```{r running the glmm}
model_1 <- glmmTMB(autotomy ~ leg * side * population + (1 | id),
                  data = df_long,
                  family = binomial)

summary (model_1)

```

(0.0) eu acho que deu efeito significativo para a perna 2 e para a pop MC (*shocked*)

```{r testing the residuals - DHARMa}
res <- simulateResiduals(model_1, plot = T)
testZeroInflation(res)
```

aqui eu to meio :P por causa dessa linha vermelha q ta basicamente horizontal, mas o DHARMa ta acusando ela vermelha, irei lindamente ignorar pois os outros teste estavam lindos (0~0)

```{r testando separadamente e excluindo cada um}
drop1(model_1, test = "Chisq")
model_2 <- glmmTMB(autotomy ~ leg + side + population + (1 | id),
                  data = df_long,
                  family = binomial)
#indicou que nenhuma interação foi relevante
drop1(model_2, test = "Chisq")
#indicou que somente as variáveis leg e population foram relevantes o que condiz com o resultado do glmmm do model_1
```

```{r testando qual perna e qual população foi diferente}
emmeans(model_2, pairwise ~ leg, type = "response")
emmeans(model_2, pairwise ~ population, type = "response")
```
